question: Can reference PyTorch Lloyd reductions be phase-batched across the 12 equal-shape layers strongly enough to close the remaining exact B64/L16 systems gap?
mathematical_identity: For layer b and code k, flattening assignments as b*K+k makes one index_add and one bincount compute exactly the same independent per-layer sufficient statistics as 12 serial calls; no observation can contribute to another layer's centroid.
frozen_oracle: Generate deterministic finite production-shape FP32 rows from the sealed source tensor without training.
Compare 12 or 24 serial reference fits with a batched torch.searchsorted plus offset-index_add/bincount fit.
Measure synchronized CUDA time after one warmup and three timed repetitions.
Record peak allocated memory and final centroid/code differences.

systems_gate.rationale: At the current calibration, the exact model needs about 1269.23 ms/update; with 740.05 ms forward/backward and non-optimizer overhead unchanged, optimizer/retraction must fall from 679.60 ms to roughly 495 ms or below.

decision_rule.correctness_pass_but_projected_optimizer: Reject before optimizer refactor; derive a persistent-kernel or cadence-neutral alternative.
decision_rule.correctness_and_projected_speed_pass: Preregister and implement a two-phase optimizer refactor, then repeat exact state/equivalence/MFU gates before any quality run.
